report:
Contrary to the assumption that honey is ineffective, medical evidence and pediatric guidelines indicate that **honey does help reduce acute cough symptoms in children over one year of age**.

### Key Findings and Evidence

* **Systematic Reviews:** A 2018 Cochrane Systematic Review evaluated randomized controlled trials and found that honey reduces cough frequency and severity better than no treatment, placebo, or diphenhydramine, while also improving sleep quality for children and parents (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD007094_honey-acute-cough-children).
* **Clinical Trials:** A clinical trial published in *Pediatrics* demonstrated that a single nocturnal dose of honey significantly decreased cough severity and frequency compared to supportive care or placebo (https://publications.aap.org/pediatrics/article/130/3/465/30142/Effect-of-Honey-on-Nocturnal-Cough-and-Sleep).
* **Medical Guidelines:** Both the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) and the American Academy of Family Physicians recommend honey as a safe, effective home remedy for coughs in children over 12 months, noting it is preferable to over-the-counter cough syrups, which lack proven efficacy in young children (https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/chest-lungs/Pages/Coughs-and-Colds-Medicines-or-Home-Remedies.aspx; https://www.aafp.org/afp/2016/0701/p20).

### Critical Safety Warning
Honey must **never** be given to infants under 12 months of age due to the risk of infant botulism, a potentially life-threatening bacterial infection.

### Conclusion
For children older than 1 year, evidence supports using honey (typically 2.5 to 5 mL) as an effective and safe treatment for acute viral cough.
